answer: A council auctions a fixed number of slots for proposals on moving saffron from the wharf to the meadow. It verifies bids and payment, rejects invalid bids, and assigns at most one slot per winning bid; replaying a bid under another alias wins no second slot. Extra influence requires another winning bid and payment, potentially at a low price. Wealth can dominate the auction, and a seller who controls the auction can manipulate allocations.
